Foodwise: Qingdao
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Eva May venture to Qingdao, China's beer mecca by the sea. With red tiles and green trees that make up the city's stunning scenery, our hosts embark on another foodie-journey with local delicacies and interesting guest appearances. From drinking beer with a German friend, catching crabs by the ocean and devouring grilled eel the classic Korean way, this episode will leave you hungry for more!

programs.desc: A Bite of Shunde tells the stories of Shunde locals through food, showcasing this city's heritage and present-day life. It looks at the craftsmanship Shunde people apply in the kitchen and beyond, and the dedicated, artisan mentality behind their renowned culinary culture. Through their attitude toward a simple home-cooked meal, we get insights into their values and way of life.

Ride the trails, unlock Chongli's rhythm
programs.desc: Chongli in Zhangjiakou, north China's Hebei Province, first made its name with Winter Olympic ski runs. Now, with cool summers and a wealth of outdoor activities, this mountain town is writing a new summer chapter. CGTN host Julian Waghann and Mexican traveler Juan Carlos Cheang Guzman came to explore. They tried mountain biking and discovered the sustainable model of "winter skiing, summer cycling." At an ultra-trail race, runners pressed forward through pouring rain, their headlamps flickering like stars across the night. The Olympics may have ended, but the venues are far from dormant. They power new vitality for Chongli's all-season sports and cultural tourism.

Foodwise: Datong
programs.desc: In this episode, Tianran He and Angela Fu are in historic Datong. Located in northern China's Shanxi Province, some 1500 years ago Datong was the capital of the Northern Wei Dynasty, which saw nomads unite northern China and Buddhism spread throughout the country. At the renowned Yungang Grottoes where giant Buddhas were carved out of cliffs, our hosts discover Datong's multicultural past and sample the emperor's favorite cake. They seek out the remains of a Jesuit church beneath the Great Wall of China, and find in the local cuisine elements that echo the past, and modern-day recipes for thousand-year old dishes.

programs.title: China IRL: Beijing Hutongs
programs.desc: Jack, Alex and Tianran wander Beijing's historic laneways, taking in traditional sweets, historical views, and a centuries-old kite-making tradition. Reflecting on the coexistence of ancient customs and hyper-modern life, they climb Beihai Park's iconic white stupa to enjoy an "emperor's view" below.

programs.title: Kung Fu Wise II-3 Shaolin Style
programs.desc: Episode 3, Shaolin, explores how this thousand-year-old temple has evolved into a unique "kung fu platform" that draws enthusiasts from around the world. Host Kleber immerses himself in Shaolin's integrated way of life, where Chan (Zen) practice and martial training go hand in hand, and turns the camera toward foreign practitioners pursuing their kung fu dreams both inside and beyond the temple gates. Along the way, he meets international disciples living and training at Shaolin, as well as students learning the rare art of Shaolin Xinyiba under Master Hu Zhengsheng, a former Shaolin monk. At martial arts schools near Songshan Mountain, Kleber also encounters overseas competitors training hard for the arena. Together, their stories reveal Shaolin kung fu's enduring pull, one that crosses cultures and borders while uniting practitioners through tradition, discipline, and self-mastery.

programs.title: China Untapped: Changsha
programs.desc: The city of Changsha is one of central China's powerhouses. It's a leader in both the construction machinery industry and in media - Changsha was China's first UNESCO "Creative City". It's also one of China's best-known cities for its nightlife. The soul of a city is in its people, and this episode focuses on the women of Changsha who are helping to innovate, change and further develop this city they call home.

programs.title: Tales in Light and Shadow
programs.desc: Beijing shadow puppets bring ancient Chinese tales to life with intricately crafted leather figures. Behind an illuminated screen, these colorful silhouettes dance, enacting epic stories and folklore accompanied by traditional music. Discover this captivating performing art, a cherished part of China's rich cultural tapestry and a mesmerizing visual spectacle.

programs.title: A Bite of Dongguan Ep.1
programs.desc: An exploration of authentic urban cuisine, this documentary unveils the hidden culinary world beneath the surface of Dongguan - an international city with a deeply rooted food culture.

programs.title: Fujian's Tulou - The Mysterious Earthen Castles
programs.desc: The tulous, or earth-built dwellings, of Fujian are recognized as treasures of traditional architecture, thanks to their unique design, cultural importance, and embodiment of the concept of harmonious coexistence with nature. Tulous are mostly rectangular or circular in form, with a simple, elegant exterior and a well-furnished interior. As homes built by the Hakka people, they are imbued with diligence, wisdom, and the pursuit of excellence. Surrounded by mountains and waters, the tulous blend well with the natural environment. When building their tulous, the Hakka people pay attention to ecological balance in order to minimize their environmental footprint. A tulou is not only a safe place to live, but also the crystallization of the culture and architectural skill passed down for generations among the Hakka people.

programs.title: China Bound: Wuhan
programs.desc: Tianran He visits Wuhan, a megacity at the crossroads of central China. From experiencing its vibrant breakfast culture and iconic dishes like hot dry noodles to exploring the lakes and hills of the expansive East Lake, as well as historic districts that showcase a blend of Chinese and Western architecture, Tianran uncovers why Wuhan has been a pivotal city in Chinese history for centuries. Finally, he relives some of these moments through immersive theater performances set amongst historic buildings and aboard a steamship cruising the Yangtze River.
